title: feat(spec,cli): `description` is authorable on an action — the mechanism for #7278/#7309 (#7367)
body:
Closes #7367

Implements the mechanism for the maintainer's 2026-08-10 ruling on #7278, quoted verbatim and untranslated in that card:

> "Drop `confirmText` from `approval_reject` and `approval_recall`; the param dialog carries the confirm question as its description — one condition, one wording, one dialog, nothing sent until its own Confirm. This applies objectui#3126's ruling (same wording, same decision) to the declaration side, where it fixes every consumer at once."

An action may now declare a top-level `description`, I18nLabel-shaped exactly as `label`. This is a **producer** gap being closed, not a renderer gap: the consumer chain shipped long ago and has been unreachable.

## Premise — re-verified on this branch's merge base, not inherited from triage

Triage anchored the premise at `60f0dd8`; I re-anchored it by content on `origin/main` @ `18ff1dab1`, probing the real rebuilt schemas rather than reading the source.

| Claim in the card | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionSchema` refuses a top-level `description` | **CONFIRMED** | `safeParse` → `unrecognized_keys`: "Unrecognized key(s) on this action: `description`." Both the string and the `{ en, zh-CN }` forms. |
| `actionTranslationSchema` refuses it | **CONFIRMED** | Refused at **both** addresses — `objects.{o}._actions.{a}` and `globalActions.{a}` — "Unrecognized key(s) on this object action translation / this global action translation: `description`." |
| The extractor emits no action-level `description` | **CONFIRMED** | Only `label` / `confirmText` / `successMessage` / `params` / `resultDialog` at the two emission sites. |
| objectui already renders it | **CONFIRMED** | `ActionParamDialog.tsx:215` renders `state.description` as `DialogDescription`; fed by `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:206` and `RecordDetailView.tsx:586`, both `actionDescription(objForI18n, action?.name, action?.description)`; resolved by `useObjectLabel.ts:463` walking `objects.{o}._actions.{a}.description` → `globalActions.{a}.description` → the literal. (objectui @`5e52495`) |
| The `:84` alias-guidance entry needs reconciling | **RESOLVED — no change needed, see below** | |

Premise holds in full; nothing had expired.

### The `:84` alias entry — reconciled by measurement, not by edit

The card flagged that an alias hint for `description` "may exist" and must not be left claiming the key is refused. It does exist, and it is **correct as-is**: `ACTION_PARAM_KEY_ALIASES.description = 'helpText'` is on `ActionParamSchema` — the action **param** surface, one level down. A param-level `description` is still refused and `helpText` is still its canonical spelling; the key this PR legalises is on the **action**. Deleting that entry as "stale" would be the actual regression, so it is pinned instead (`an action PARAM still routes description to helpText`).

The action shape's own `guidance` map has no `description` entry — the nearby `exposed` guidance points at `ai: { exposed, description }` and is about `exposed`, not about this key. It is untouched and still accurate.

## Per-surface changes

**`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`** — optional `description: I18nLabelSchema`, declared next to `label`. The describe-prose names the render site, the i18n convention, and the two things authors will otherwise get wrong: that this carries the confirm question for a param-collecting action, and that it is **not** `ai.description` (the ≥40-char LLM tool contract, unchanged).

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — the matching `description` slot on `actionTranslationSchema`, so both addresses the resolver walks can carry it. Flat `string`, like its siblings: the bundle is already per-locale.

**`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`** — emitted at both action sites (top-level/global and inline-on-object) plus the walk-surface doc block. Kept in this PR deliberately: splitting it opens a declared-but-not-extracted window, which is the same leak objectstack#3370 closed for action labels. The CLI half turned out to be **trivial** — two `pushOptional` lines and two doc lines; no split warranted.

`pushOptional`, not `pushDerived` — matching `confirmText`, not `label`. The dialog falls back to its own generic `actionDialog.description`, so an undeclared description is not a translation gap; deriving one would seed English text nobody authored and then gate every locale on translating it.

**Train artifacts** — `authorable-surface/ui.json` gains `ui/Action:description` (generated); liveness ledger gains an `action.description` row, `status: live`, `verifiedAt: 2026-08-10`, evidence pinned to objectui @`5e52495`; generated references regenerated.

`InlineActionSchema` deliberately does **not** gain the key. That shape forwards only what a host renderer honours and "widens when a renderer widens, not before"; `element:button` has no description slot. Pinned as an invariant.

## Pins

Path + code + message, never bare success flags.

`packages/spec/src/ui/action-description.test.ts` (13):
- accepts the plain-string and localized-map forms, asserting the parsed value back;
- **contract parity with `label` asserted directly** rather than restated — six values are fed to both keys and the results compared, so a divergence in either direction fails;
- optional when absent;
- strict shape intact: an unknown sibling still refused, pinned on the **suggestion arrow** — `` Did you mean `descriptionText` → `description`? `` — not on `toContain('description')`, which would be satisfied by the substring inside `descriptionText` and stay green with the key removed;
- `ai.description` untouched, including that a top-level `description` does not satisfy `ai.exposed`;
- the two non-widened surfaces (param alias → `helpText`, inline action refusal);
- translation schema at both addresses, flat-string-only, strict-sibling refusal on the same arrow, and action-description vs `resultDialog.description` kept distinct.

`packages/cli/test/i18n-extract-action-description.test.ts` (7): emission for top-level / global / inline-on-object actions; the seeded text and `source: 'action'` attribution; coverage gating an untranslated description and going quiet once translated; and one fixture action walked **schema → extractor → translation bundle** end-to-end, asserting the three surfaces agree on one address.

### One pin was rewritten because a measurement falsified my presumption

I first asserted the extractor emits **no path at all** for an undeclared `description`. Measured: `pushOptional` on an absent value still records a **seed-less** entry (path present, `sourceValue` undefined) — deliberately, so the coverage gate can spot a bundle authoring a key the metadata never writes — and `confirmText` has always behaved identically. "The path is absent" was never the contract. The pin now asserts the real one — nothing seeded, nothing gated — plus parity with the undeclared `confirmText` beside it and the `label` contrast. This strictly improved it: the original could not catch the extractor's removal at all (green because nothing is produced), the rewrite does.

## Reverse verification — predicted in writing before running, both directions

Two independent halves ship here, so two reverts. Direction predicted per pin **before** either was run, including which must stay GREEN as invariants.

**Direction A — revert the schema half** (`git checkout origin/main -- action.zod.ts translation.zod.ts`, spec rebuilt so the CLI's `dist` resolution is honest too):

| | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| spec pins | 10 RED / 3 GREEN | **10 RED / 3 GREEN** |
| cli pins | 1 RED / 6 GREEN | **1 RED / 6 GREEN** |

The 10 reds are exactly the ones named in advance; the 3 spec greens are the predicted invariants (optional-when-absent, param alias → `helpText`, inline refusal), and the 6 cli greens are the extractor pins, which walk raw config objects and never touch `ActionSchema` — that independence is the design, not an accident.

**Direction B — revert the extractor half only:**

| | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| spec pins | all GREEN | **13 GREEN** |
| cli pins | 7 RED | **7 RED** |

Every per-pin direction was called correctly in both runs (20/20 and 20/20). Two corrections in the interest of not overclaiming: my prediction file's **totals lines** were arithmetically off by one in each direction (I wrote 7 and 12 GREEN where the tables imply 9 and 13 — I collapsed three "emits" tests into one table row and miscounted the spec file); the per-pin tables themselves were right. And the direction-B figure is post-amendment — the rewritten seed-less pin moved from predicted-GREEN to predicted-RED, recorded before the run, not after.

No single revert turns everything red: the two halves are pinned separately, so a future change removing one cannot be masked by the other's tests.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:generated` | **11/11 up to date** (`check:docs` was stale after the describe-prose; regenerated with `gen:docs`, nothing else) |
| spec suite | **364 files passed** |
| cli suite | **108 files / 1162 tests passed** |
| `typecheck` (spec + cli) | passed, incl. `check:scripts-typecheck` + `check:test-typecheck` |
| `check:liveness` | green — **355 repo-local evidence paths declared, 355 resolved** |
| `check-adr-0087-registration` | **0 declared-breaking changesets** |
| `check-nul-bytes` | OK, 6767 files; plus a control-byte self-scan of every file this PR touches — clean |

Four-step regen ran with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` **first** (the #7122 trap). No export moved, so `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` stayed green and no dual-snapshot was needed.

One gate finding worth recording, because it cost a lap: the liveness evidence parser attributes a realm marker only **up to the next `;`**. My first evidence string said `objectui @5e52495 — …; fed by …; resolver …`, so everything after the first semicolon was read as repo-local and three objectui paths were reported as rot. Re-marking each clause fixed it. The README documents the rule; the failure mode is easy to walk into when the evidence cites several files.

Neither `content/docs/releases/` nor `docs/adr/**` was touched, and no gate asked for either.

## Changeset

`@objectstack/spec`: **minor**, `@objectstack/cli`: patch. Minor per precedent for an additive optional authorable key (it enlarges the legal-metadata set — third-party API surface for this platform — while every existing action, bundle and extract keeps parsing unchanged). Nothing breaking; `check-adr-0087-registration` confirms 0 declared-breaking.

## Item 5 — filed, not folded in, with the census measured

The card's item 5 (a schema-level warn/refuse on the `confirmText` + `params` **pair**) is filed as a follow-up rather than shipped here, and the measurement is why. I censused the pair across the repo: **20 shipped sites** with `confirmText` beside a non-empty `params` — consistent with #7309's "18 more", and it includes the four showcase-app actions that card does not count.

A refusal would break all 20 before their migration. A **warn**-severity arm does not qualify for the "zero shipped-metadata breakage" exception either: it would fire on 20 declarations, 16 of them the platform's own `platform-objects`, i.e. warnings on every build of an untouched project. The guard is right, but it belongs **after** #7278 and #7309 migrate, not before — so it is filed standalone with `Blocked-by:` lines rather than as a sub-issue, since it merely depends on those cards rather than falling inside their completion scope.

Full census in the follow-up: #7428.

## Unlocks

#7278 and #7309 become two-line moves once this lands (`confirmText` → `description`). Posting the unlock notes there is the PM's step, not this PR's.
